chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from the one whom he mentioned, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, from Dāwūd ibn al-Qāsim, who said:
I heard Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام saying: “The successor after me is al-Ḥasan. So how will it be for you regarding the successor after the successor?”
So I said: “And why, may Allah make me your ransom?” He said: “You will not see his person, and it will not be permissible for you to mention him by his name.”
So I said: “Then how should we mention him?” He said: “Say: al-Ḥujjah from the family of Muḥammad عليهم السلام.”

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ: al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, identified here as the successor after the speaker
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: the Divine Authority, a title of the Imam
key_terms.الْخَلَفُ: the successor who comes after a preceding Imam
key_terms.شَخْصَهُ: his person or visible physical presence

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith from al-Kāfī describe the successor after Imam al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the succession of al-Ḥasan عليه السلام after Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and then alludes to the Imam who comes after him. It states that the later successor would not be seen openly and that people should refer to him as al-Ḥujjah from the family of Muḥammad عليهم السلام rather than by his personal name. The narration is significant in Shia doctrine for its indication of the concealed Imam and the etiquette of referring to him.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Alawy, from Dawood Bin Al Qasim who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The replacement (Imam<sup>asws</sup>) from after me<sup>asws</sup> is Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. So how would it be for you all with the replacement (Imam<sup>asws</sup>) from after the replacement (Imam<sup>asws</sup>)?’

So I said, ‘And why (would it be so)? May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make me to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You all would not be seeing his<sup>asws</sup> person (physically), nor would it be Permissible for you all to mention him<sup>asws</sup> by his<sup>asws</sup> name’.

So I said, ‘So how should be mention him<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be saying, ‘الْحُجَّةُ مِنْ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ’ ‘The Divine Authority (Al-Hujjat) from the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from the person he mentioned from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-‘Alawi from Dawud ibn al-Qasim who has said the following.
“I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) saying, ‘The succeeding (Imam) after me will be al-Hassan. How will your dealing be with the succeeding (Imam) of the succeeding (Imam)?”
I then said, “Why will that be so, may Allah take my souls in service for your cause?” He said, “You will not see him in person. It will not lawful for you to pronounce his name.”
I then asked, “How then will we speak of him?” He said, “Say, ‘The Divine Authority from the family of Muhammad (s.a).”
